picked.t: Widespread flooding disrupts traffic, business in Hanoi after heavy rain overnight
picked.body: Rainfall recorded from 7 p.m. Wednesday to 3 a.m. Thursday reached 199 mm in Tu Liem, 190 mm in Hai Ba Trung, 182 mm in Cau Giay, 164 mm in Yen So and 153 mm in Thanh Liet, according to the Hanoi Sewerage Company. Floodwaters of 30-50 centimeters covered numerous roads, while some low-lying areas were submerged by nearly a meter. Several major routes became difficult or impossible for vehicles to pass, leaving motorists stranded in long traffic queues and forcing others to seek higher ground. On some roads, water covered most of the street surface, with authorities restricting traffic in flooded sections. Vehicles were forced to move slowly through deep water, while some stalled and required assistance. The flooding was particularly severe in western and southwestern parts of the city, including Tay Mo and nearby areas. Some streets were submerged by 30-50 cm, while Cau Coc Street was covered by more than half a meter of water and nearly one meter in some sections. Flooding also disrupted public services and daily routines. Some schools closed or switched to online classes, while residents skipped work because of impassable roads. In several neighborhoods, people moved goods and vehicles to higher ground to protect them from rising water. The disruption extended to major traffic corridors across the city, with severe congestion reported as vehicles were diverted toward higher ground. Some commuters abandoned their vehicles or pushed stalled motorbikes through the water. Central areas experienced less severe flooding. Some streets had drained by around 8:40 a.m., while localized flooding in other areas cleared later in the morning. The Hanoi Construction Department said continuous rain since Sept. 14 had brought cumulative rainfall above 400 mm in many parts of the city and above 500 mm in several areas. The Nhue River and its tributaries were at alarm levels, while high downstream water levels restricted natural drainage. By 12:40 p.m., 36 pumping stations were operating at maximum capacity. Water levels were gradually receding in some flooded areas, including Phu Dien, Tu Liem and Nghia Do, where flooding had earlier reached 30-40 cm. However, low-lying areas of the Nhue River basin, particularly Tay Mo and Xuan Phuong, remained flooded. The National Center for Hydro-Meteorological Forecasting warned of thunderstorms in the following hours, with possible tornadoes, lightning, strong wind gusts and hail. The heavy rain was attributed to the interaction between a tropical depression and the intertropical convergence zone, which brought continuous rainfall to Hanoi from Sept. 14 to 17.

picked.t: Southeast Asia's most populous metropolis ranks its 2nd smartest city
picked.body: In the inaugural Intelligent Cities Index 2026, released by global consulting firm Boston Consulting Group (BCG), the city state of Singapore ranked highest in Southeast Asia and 11th globally. It was followed by Jakarta, which ranked 39th worldwide. The Indonesian capital is the most populous city in Southeast Asia with 42 million people, according to an estimate by the U.N. Department of Economic and Social Affairs' Population Division in its World Urbanization Prospects 2025 report. The city even overtook Tokyo to become the world's most populous city last year, according to a United Nations study. Vietnam's most populous city, Ho Chi Minh, ranked 48th globally, making it the third smartest city in Southeast Asia, followed closely by Malaysia's capital, Kuala Lumpur, at 50th. No other Southeast Asian countries are ranked. The index evaluates how 61 major cities across 39 countries use artificial intelligence and digital technologies to serve residents and businesses across five areas: resident outcomes, intelligent city strategy, technology adoption, ways of working, and enabling factors such as infrastructure, talent and funding. The world's five leading cities are London, Dubai, New York City, Washington, D.C., and Amsterdam. BCG said the index shows that artificial intelligence is becoming a key foundation of intelligent cities. Cities with higher levels of AI adoption tend to have more use cases and deliver better outcomes for residents. Rather than focusing solely on technology infrastructure, the index examines how effectively cities turn digital capabilities into better services and quality of life. BCG said technology alone is not enough, with successful cities also requiring effective governance, funding, talent, infrastructure and innovation ecosystems. The report found that cities where residents use smart-city applications more frequently also tend to report higher satisfaction. London and Dubai, for example, combine high usage with strong satisfaction among app users. BCG also identified different paths for cities seeking to improve their intelligent-city maturity. Some succeed by developing balanced capabilities across multiple areas, while others focus on particular strengths such as strategy, governance, partnerships, infrastructure or talent. For cities seeking to advance, BCG recommends clarifying long-term priorities, improving governance and partnerships, expanding proven AI and digital services, and investing in data, technology, infrastructure and skills. The report said AI adoption can improve resident outcomes even in cities that have not yet developed world-class infrastructure or funding ecosystems. This suggests cities can begin by expanding practical AI-enabled services while building broader capabilities over time.

picked.t: 3 Vietnamese restaurants earn platinum status in global fine dining list
picked.body: The list indicates the growing international recognition of Vietnam's fine dining scene. Founded in 2016 as part of China's largest online travel platform Trip.com, Trip.Gourmet is a one-stop food guide, offering global restaurant rankings, travel-focused food content, and reservation options. This year's selection, published on Sept. 8, has 744 restaurants in 105 cities across 40 countries. Gia Located near Hanoi's historic Temple of Literature, Gia specializes in contemporary Vietnamese cuisine. The name originates from gia dinh , meaning family in Vietnamese. Gia tells the story of local flavors and childhood traditions, reinterpreting them through a refined, modern lens while using seasonal local ingredients and modern techniques. Hibana by KOKI Situated in the renowned 5 star luxury hotel Capella Hanoi, Hibana by KOKI offers an exclusive Japanese teppanyaki experience in an intimate 14-seat setting. The venue focuses on live cooking performances by skilled chefs using premium imported ingredients. Anan Saigon In Ho Chi Minh City, Anan Saigon, named after the phrase an an , meaning "eat, eat", is located in Cho Cu on Ton That Dam Street, a wet market in the heart of the city. In the words of the restaurant, the head chef elevates street food and traditional dishes into a fine dining experience using fresh local ingredients and incorporating French culinary techniques, all while retaining essential Vietnamese flavors. Its menu features signature creations such as the banh xeo taco, Da Lat street style pizza, Mekong Delta fish, broken rice, and fish sauce ice cream. According to the Michelin Guide, all three establishments earned their first Michelin star in June 2023. Since then, Gia, Hibana by KOKI, and Anan Saigon have successfully retained their one Michelin star every year, including the awards in June 2026.

picked.t: Central Group, controlled by Thai billionaire family Chirathivat, mulls $1.5B Vietnam investment
picked.body: "This is a particularly important market for us," Wallaya Chirathivat, chairwoman of Central Group, said during a press briefing on Thursday. Central Group entered Vietnam through Central Retail in 2012, and owns a range of retail brands, including GO!, Tops Market, Lan Chi Mart, and Supersports. It currently has 330 stores and shopping malls in 26 provinces and cities. It has invested $1.5 billion in Vietnam so far. Its plans to double that investment is driven by three main factors, the first being the country's rapid economic growth with GDP growing at 8-10% annually, outperforming the regional average, according to Chirathivat. Vietnam's population has surpassed 100 million, much larger than Thailand's, with consumers willing to shop through modern retail channels, she added. The economy also has a broad geographic structure stretching all the way from north to south, offering room for development across provinces and cities, she said. "We have cooperation agreements with Sun Group and other local businesses to research and develop projects," she said, referring to one of Vietnam's leading resort developers known for building landmarks and theme parks. Olivier Langlet, CEO of Central Retail Vietnam, said the investment plan would focus primarily on retail and shopping malls along with hotels. The company has identified 200 locations in urban areas for further study, he said. "Our team is very busy looking for suitable locations and land plots to develop projects. This is a very large workload." In the hotel business, in addition to the 984-room Centara Mirage Resort Mui Ne in Lam Dong, which has been operating since 2020, the company is developing two more properties in China-bordering Quang Ninh city, which will add about 1,000 rooms. Langlet said one challenge facing the proposal is that land in Vietnam has become "very expensive," requiring the company to carefully calculate its investments to ensure returns meet shareholders' expectations. Besides, while Vietnam has greatly simplified administrative procedures, it needs further improvements since some regulations remain ambiguous, making it difficult for investors to navigate through them. Central Retail's revenues in Vietnam in the first half of the year were more than 24 billion Thai baht (US$722 million), according to its financial report. This accounted for 20% of the company's overall revenues, making Vietnam its second largest market after Thailand. The Chirathivat family ranked fourth in Thailand's 50 Richest list compiled by Forbes this year. It has been in the list for nine years in a row.

By the morning, many monitoring stations had recorded more than 150 mm of rain. With traffic paralyzed on Road 70 in Tay Mo Ward, a young man ferries people by boat across a flooded stretch of about 500 m for VND50,000 ($1.92). picked.t: Sanofi, VNVC sign joint declaration on next-generation vaccine manufacturing in Vietnam
picked.body: Sanofi Vietnam and VNVC signed a joint declaration on strategic cooperation in next-generation vaccine manufacturing in Vietnam at the Vietnam-France Business Forum in Paris on Sept. 10. The forum brought together businesses from the two countries, with the participation of Vietnam's Party General Secretary and President To Lam, French President Emmanuel Macron, and senior officials from both countries. Under the declaration, Sanofi and VNVC will work to strengthen Vietnam's domestic vaccine manufacturing capacity, increase supply autonomy, and address disease prevention needs. The cooperation also covers healthcare access, workforce development, and building a sustainable vaccine ecosystem. The companies are identifying vaccines for potential future production by VNVC, with three initially selected for further assessment. Following the signing, representatives of Vietnam's Ministry of Health, VNVC, and Sanofi visited Sanofi's manufacturing facility in Neuville-sur-Saône, France, to learn about its manufacturing technologies, expertise and quality systems and discuss the cooperation roadmap. The three vaccines identified as priorities are intended to address areas of high unmet demand and support disease prevention across different age groups, from infants and adolescents to adults and the elderly. VNVC plans to complete and put its Vaccine and Biologics Manufacturing Facility into operation by the end of 2027. The first vaccine batches are targeted for production in 2028, with vaccines manufactured in Vietnam expected to be commercialized from 2029. The partnership has developed through several stages, including a milestone during French President Emmanuel Macron's visit to Vietnam in 2025. The September 2026 declaration marks a further step, with the companies identifying specific product priorities and milestones for potential local vaccine manufacturing. Stephen Alix, Head of Vaccines, International at Sanofi, said the company supports Vietnam's efforts to advance science and technology, innovation and high-tech industries while strengthening its healthcare system. "With more than 70 years of presence in Vietnam, Sanofi deeply values the direction set by the Communist Party and Government of Vietnam in advancing science and technology, fostering innovation, developing high-tech industries, and strengthening the resilience of the national healthcare system," Alix said. "Through this initiative, Sanofi seeks to make a meaningful contribution to the country's goals and to the development of an increasingly advanced biotechnology ecosystem in Vietnam." Ngo Chi Dung, Chairman and General Director of VNVC, said the declaration marked a shift from outlining areas of cooperation toward implementing plans to localize next-generation vaccine manufacturing in Vietnam. VNVC's Vaccine and Biologics Manufacturing Facility in Tay Ninh has an initial investment of more than VND2.5 trillion (US$96.18 million) and covers over 26,000 square meters. The facility is designed to produce about 120 million vaccine doses a year and aims to meet international standards, including WHO-GMP, EU-GMP, and FDA-cGMP. VNVC said the project is intended to strengthen domestic capabilities in vaccine and biologics research, manufacturing and testing.

picked.t: Tech workers spiral into anxiety, exhaustion because of 'age 35 curse'
picked.body: With no family dependents or debt to speak of, the Ho Chi Minh City programmer has nevertheless driven himself to total exhaustion for nearly two years. Beyond regular business hours, he works as a freelancer, taking on web design and software outsourcing contracts for clients across various time zones, leaving his desk strewn with half-eaten takeout containers and empty soda cans. "Every time a tech firm announces layoffs driven by automation, a chill runs down my spine," he says. Vietnamese tech workers are facing growing anxiety and burnout as layoffs, artificial intelligence and the industry's "age 35 curse" intensify pressure to keep working and upgrading their skills. Facing that same fear of obsolescence, Hoang Nam, a 34-year-old security engineer based in the southern province of Tay Ninh, also has a mortgage of over VND1 billion (US$40,000) and two young children. His company recently restructured, cutting nearly 20% of junior programming roles and replacing humans with automated coding tools. To safeguard his job, Nam took on extra in-house responsibilities while staying up late for freelance projects and teaching himself new machine learning tools. But after spending 15 hours a day staring at screens, his blood pressure consistently hovers above 140/90 mmHg. "Catching my reflection in the mirror at 3:00 a.m., with sunken eyes and a pounding heart, I know full well I'm destroying my body," Nam says. "But stopping now means losing my income and being replaced overnight by fresh graduates and younger coders." Terrified by the looming threat of a stroke, he checked into a hospital and was diagnosed with dyslipidemia, hypertension, prediabetes, and mild depression, all requiring long-term medical treatment. While nationwide figures remain unrecorded, the ordeal shared by Vinh and Nam dominates conversations across Vietnamese online tech communities. A persistent wave of layoffs in the industry, compounded by a desperate race to master emerging tools like AI is pushing software developers into chronic burnout. Clinicians are seeing the fallout firsthand. Medical professionals caution that the cohort of tech workers seeking treatment for chronic insomnia, physical collapse, and metabolic disorders is skewing dramatically younger. In its International Classification of Diseases (ICD-11), the World Health Organization defines burnout as an occupational syndrome resulting from chronic workplace stress that has not been successfully managed. The condition is marked by three core dimensions: energy depletion, growing mental detachment or cynicism toward one's job, and a steep decline in professional efficacy. Hoang Tien Trong Nghia, head of the neurology department at Ho Chi Minh City-based Military Hospital 175, says relentless stress triggers systemic inflammation and autonomic nervous dysfunction, significantly elevating the risk of cardiovascular disease, atherosclerosis, and strokes among younger adults. "Clinical practice has recently seen a surge in cases of hypertension, cardiac arrhythmia, and nervous breakdowns in patients under 35. "Nearly all of them have the same habits: hours of sedentary screen time, heavy reliance on stimulants like caffeine to pull all-nighters, and working under constant anxiety." Compounding this physical toll is a longstanding industry dread across Asian tech markets known as the "age 35 curse," or older professionals being stereotyped as slow to adapt, overly expensive due to seniority, and unable to keep pace with brutal overtime hours accepted by their younger colleagues. A 2024 tech recruitment survey by platform TopDev found that nearly 70% of Vietnamese tech companies prefer hiring engineers under 30 for frontline development roles to rein in payroll costs and maintain operational agility. That has only intensified as generative AI sweeps the tech landscape. Global layoff tracker Layoffs.fyi counted over 150,000 tech job cuts worldwide over the past year, heavily hitting baseline programming and quality assurance testing, tasks that automated algorithms can easily perform. Yet, from an employer's perspective, this weeding-out process is not merely about a number on a birth certificate. Nguyen Tuan Anh, chief technology officer at a Ho Chi Minh City software firm, argues that companies do not let people go simply because they turned 35, but rather because they "stopped delivering new value." Many professionals confuse a decade of growth with a single year of experience repeated 10 times over. As AI slashes the time needed to churn out routine code, businesses are trimming those who work mechanically, while holding on to talent that can untangle complex problems, design system architecture, and lead project delivery. "If a senior engineer cannot deliver markedly more value than a junior developer equipped with AI, they will inevitably face replacement," Anh points out. picked.t: MoMo, Saigontourist Travel partner to develop digital travel services
picked.body: Financial technology company MoMo and Saigontourist Travel, a subsidiary of Saigontourist Group, announced a strategic partnership on Sept. 18 to combine travel products with technology and payment services. Under the agreement, Saigontourist Travel will expand the distribution of its products on MoMo, while the two companies develop promotions and use data and technology to analyze customer needs and improve user experience and marketing efficiency. The partnership will also expand payment options for Vietnamese traveling abroad. MoMo supports payments in more than 60 countries and territories, including popular destinations such as China, Thailand, South Korea and Japan. In China, users can scan MoMo QR codes at more than 40 million payment points within the Alipay and WeChat networks. In Thailand, MoMo supports Thai QR, PromptPay, Alipay and VietQR Global at millions of payment locations. According to the company, these services can reduce travelers' need to carry cash or prepare additional international payment cards. The company said it uses transparent exchange rates and does not charge service fees for these transactions. MoMo and Saigontourist Group will also offer promotions linked to travel products and payments. New customers making their first QR-code payment with MoMo can currently receive discounts of up to 50%, capped at VND100,000, at eligible locations. Nguyen Ba Diep, Senior Vice President and co-founder of MoMo, said that both companies are working together to deliver a seamless customer journey, from booking tickets and accommodation to making payments at destinations. Nguyen Thanh Luu, general director of Saigontourist Travel, said the company's digital transformation covers how it studies customer needs, develops products, reaches travelers and provides services. "The partnership with MoMo combines Saigontourist Travel's brand, organizational capabilities, and travel ecosystem with MoMo's technology platform, payment capabilities, and user base," Luu said. MoMo has around 30 million users, while Saigontourist Travel has operated in the travel industry for about half a century. The partnership will also combine MoMo's technology, user base and payment infrastructure with Saigontourist Travel's experience in tour operations and travel products, with a focus on product distribution, promotions, data applications and payment services.

picked.t: Hanoi restaurant makes world's top 3 fine dining list
picked.body: Tripadvisor makes the ranking by weighing culinary artistry, elegant ambiance, and service quality against international standards. The Rhythms is set on the 7th floor of La Sinfonía del Rey Hotel & Spa in Hanoi's Old Quarter that blends western neoclassical architecture with traditional Vietnamese cultural touches. Its menu takes humble, everyday dishes and pan-Vietnamese specialties and turns them into refined dining experiences, pairing fresh local ingredients with modern culinary techniques. It has a perfect 5/5 rating from more than 2,300 reviews on the platform, with international diners frequently praising its nuanced flavors and views overlooking the heart of the capital. Vietnam's presence in the list of world's top fine dining venues reflects its growing stature on the global culinary map. In recent years, it has repeatedly emerged as a bright spot in international gastronomy. The Michelin Guide's 2025 edition named a record 181 restaurants across Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City, and Da Nang, nine of them one-starred. Hanoi also won the "World's Best Culinary City Destination" at the 2024 World Culinary Awards. Topping this year's Tripadvisor list is Fogón Asado in Buenos Aires, Argentina, a steakhouse celebrated for its traditional wood-fired grilling experience. Singapore's KOMA took second place, while The Witchery in Edinburgh, Scotland, was fourth. The "World's Best Fine Dining Restaurants" ranking is part of Tripadvisor's annual Travelers' Choice Best of the Best Restaurants awards. The rankings are determined by an algorithm analyzing the volume and quality of reviews, alongside authentic feedback from the global travel community over a 12-month period.

picked.t: 베트남, ‘두리안값’ 최고 30% 큰 폭 반등…견조한 수요 속 공급 감소 영향
picked.body: 호치민시의 한 디저트 가게에서 판매 중인 두리안. 최근 몇 달간 풍부한 공급에 급락세를 보였던 두리안 가격이 큰 폭으로 반등했다. 업계에 따르면, 일부 창고에서 거래되는 고급 두리안의 가격은 kg당 10만 동까지 치솟았다. 이전과 비교하면 20~30% 상승한 수준이다. 업계에 따르면 두리안 주산지인 닥락성(Dak Lak) 일부 저장창고에서는 선별된 고급 몬통 두리안이 kg당 10만~10만5,000동(3.9~4달러)에 거래되고 있다. 등급별로는 A급 두리안이 9만~9만5,000동(3.5~3.7달러), B급이 6만~7만 동(2.3~2.7달러)으로 지난달보다 20~30% 오른 상태다. 5월 초부터 풍부한 공급에 창고가 kg당 6만 동, 산지가는 4만5,000~5만 동(1.7~1.9달러)까지 떨어지며 수개월간 약세를 보였던 두리안 가격은 중부 고원 외 지역에서 수확이 끝나자 다시금 강한 반등을 나타내고 있다. 최근 몇 주 사이 두리안 가격 급등은 주로 공급이 감소한 데 기인했다. 업계에 따르면, 닥락성에서 수확이 한창인 가운데 농가별 수확량은 고르지 않으며, 악천후로 인해 일부 수확물은 품질 기준을 충족하지 못해 고급 두리안 공급이 감소세를 보이고 있다. 이러한 가운데 중국의 두리안 수요 증가는 가격 상승세를 부추기고 있다. 닥락성두리안협회는 “수출업체들이 중국의 중추절과 국경절(10월 1일)을 앞두고 물량 확보전에 나서고 있다. 시장 공급이 부족해지면서 두리안 가격도 상승세를 나타내고 있다”고 설명했다. 그러나 예상 수확량이 아직 상당한 만큼, 추가적으로 큰 폭의 상승세는 제한적일 것으로 예상된다. 협회에 따르면, 현재 닥락성 수확량은 전체 생산량의 약 40% 수준에 그치며, 11월 중하순까지 안정적인 공급이 이어질 전망이다. 올해 닥락성 두리안 생산량은 약 50만 톤에 달할 것으로 예상된다. 이는 전년 대비 약 20% 증가한 것으로, 수확철 후반 수요와 실제 수확량에 따라 두리안 가격은 지속적인 변동세를 나타낼 전망이다. 협회는 “수확철 후반부로 갈수록 계속되는 비가 두리안 품질에 영향을 줄 수 있다”며 “각 농가는 가격 변동에 대비해 안정적인 구매력을 갖춘 신뢰할 수 있는 수출업체와의 계약을 우선시해야 할 것”이라고 조언했다.
